selection_rationale: Candidate-2026-003 (RAG poisoning robustness) offers the strongest combination of novelty, direct relevance to NetOps safety, and feasible experimental scope for an IEEE/IFIP CNSM short paper. It addresses an underexplored, high-impact unresolved question (poisoning of retrieval-augmented NetOps pipelines), has clear, falsifiable outcomes (dose–response misconfiguration rates), and the required ethical/engineering repairs are concrete and manageable prior to preregistration. Compared with alternatives, it targets an adversarial threat class of immediate operational concern while avoiding human-subject complexity and heavy production-deployment risks.
unresolved_uncertainties: Appropriate, realistic bounds for poisoning strength that reflect plausible attacker capabilities in NetOps contexts
Sensitivity of results to retrieval-system choices (retriever model, k, scoring/normalization) and their interaction with poisoning—may alter effect sizes
Risk that defense tuning (filters/provenance thresholds) will require held-out validation to avoid optimistic estimates
Compute and model-call budget adequacy for covering poison-dose grid and confidence intervals at planned sample sizes
Containment sufficiency: ensuring poison artifacts remain confined to synthetic corpora and cannot be mistaken for or contaminate public datasets
required_repairs_before_preregistration: Constrain all adversarial/poison artifacts to synthetic, non-public corpora; document containment, retention, and deletion policies
Preregister the retrieval-system architecture and every hyperparameter affecting retrieval (retriever model/version, embedding/scoring method, k, reranking, similarity thresholds)
Preregister the poison-generation protocol, threat model bounds, and poison-strength dosing schedule (how poison fraction is defined and sampled)
Use held-out tuning partitions for any defense hyperparameter selection; do not tune defenses on the test set
Provide reproducible poison-seeding and retrieval-replay scripts, and log provenance metadata for every retrieved fragment

Specify safe-handling and disclosure text for potential downstream reuse or publication of poison examples (redacted or syntheticized), and obtain any required institutional oversight or ethics sign-off for adversarial-data creation
